state.name: North Carolina
state.peak_intrusion_season: March through May for spring raccoon and squirrel litters and snakes active at 60 degrees and above, May 1 through July 31 for the bat pup season when evictions pause, and September through November as raccoons, squirrels, and rodents seek winter shelter
state.climate_factor: North Carolina runs humid subtropical in the Piedmont and Coastal Plain, with mild coastal winters that keep snakes and armadillos active later into the year, genuinely cold mountain winters with bat hibernation, and hurricane-season flooding June through November that pushes snakes, raccoons, and alligators into coastal neighborhoods
state.permit_note: North Carolina requires a Wildlife Control Agent (WCA) license under G.S. 113-273(l) and 15A NCAC 10H .1501-.1510 for paid wildlife damage control and removal, including bat eviction; work runs through depredation permits, relocating trapped Carnivora, armadillos, groundhogs, nutria, and beaver is prohibited under 15A NCAC 10B .0106, and a WCA cannot issue depredation permits for listed species, big game, or bats

Alamance County.region: central Piedmont along the Haw River
Alamance County.nearest_metro: Graham is the county's own center
Alamance County.habitat_type: Piedmont suburbs and small towns with brick ranches, crawlspace foundations, and mature oak canopy over wooded lots
Alamance County.regional_wildlife: copperheads — in many Piedmont neighborhoods the only venomous snake — work ivy, leaf litter, and stone walls, while raccoons and squirrels run the oak canopy straight onto roofs
Alamance County.absent_or_rare: Armadillos have been reported in this county as their range expands east from the western mountains, but the NC Wildlife Resources Commission does not list this county among the eight with established breeding populations, so our crew treats armadillo calls here as sighting and digging reports to confirm on site rather than an established infestation. Black bears, deer, and wild turkey are big game handled by the Commission, not private removal, and listed snakes and bats cannot be taken on a WCA-issued permit.
